findings.title: Translation cache does not distinguish site fallback locales
findings.description:
The cache key includes the requested locale and backend identity, but the new fallback result also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`. Two sites sharing a process can therefore receive the same cached translation despite having different site fallback languages. Changing the default locale can likewise leave previously cached fallback results in use.

Include the effective fallback chain in the cache key, or scope and invalidate cached translations when the site's fallback configuration changes. Add regression coverage for identical translation requests under different site defaults.

findings.title: Fallback translations are loaded only for controller requests
findings.description:
The new fallback preloading runs only from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Other translation entry points do not invoke it: `Jobs::Base#perform` sets the locale directly, and `PostAlerter#create_notification` uses `I18n.with_locale`.

The accelerator still loads only `config.locale` before translating, while its patched `load_translations` disables automatic loading without explicit filenames. Consequently, a fallback locale that has not already been loaded cannot supply its translations outside the controller path. Results can depend on which locales the process previously used, and no-options translation results can then be cached.

Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary rather than only in a controller filter. Test fallback resolution from a cold backend in both request and background-job contexts.
